# Classwork 10 - Advanced ggplot Charts


## Question 1. Dumbbell Charts

```{r}
library(gapminder)
# unique(gapminder$continent)
gap_dumbbell <- gapminder::gapminder |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 2007), continent == "Americas") |> 
  select(continent, country, year, lifeExp) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = lifeExp
  ) |> 
  mutate(change = `2007` - `1952`) |>
  arrange(change)
```

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, warning=FALSE}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| eval: false
ggplot(gap_dumbbell, aes(y = fct_reorder(country,`1952`))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = `1952`,
                   xend = `2007`,
                   yend = country),
               linewidth = 1,
               color = "gray70",
               linetype = 2,
               fill = "grey85") +
 geom_segment(aes(x = `1952`,
                   xend = `2007`,
                   yend = country),
               linewidth = 1,
               color = "gray70",
               linetype = 1,
               fill = "black",
               alpha = .65) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `1952`),color = "steelblue",size = 2) +
             # size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(aes(x = `2007`),color = "darkorange",size = 2) +
             # size = 2, color = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    x = "Life expectancy (in years)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Life expectancy in 1952 vs 2007",
    subtitle = "Americas",

    # name = "year", # Legend Title

    # axis.title.x = margin(0,1,0,0)
    axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = .5),

  )
```

## Question 2. Sloph Charts

```{r}
gap_slope <- gapminder |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 2007), 
         country %in% c("United States", "Canada", "Japan") | 
           str_detect(country, "Korea")) |>
  select(country, year, gdpPercap) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year)) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarize(
    `1952` = gdpPercap[year == "1952"],
    `2007` = gdpPercap[year == "2007"]) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(change = `2007` - `1952`) |>
  slice_max(change, n = 12)

gap_slope_long <- gap_slope |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`1952`, `2007`),
               names_to = "year", values_to = "gdpPercap")
```

```{r}
gap_slope <- gapminder |> # Create Data Frame
  filter(
    year %in% c(1992, 1997, 2002, 2007), # Only use the years we need 
    country %in% c("United States", "Canada", "Puerto Rico",
                   "Mexico", "Nicaragua", "El Salvador") # Filter to only have the countries we need for the plot
  ) |>
  select(country, year, lifeExp) |> # Pinpoint the 3 columns needed 
  mutate(year = factor(year)) |> # Create the variable 
  group_by(country) |> # Do calculations to each country separately 
  summarize(
    `1992` = lifeExp[year == "1992"],
    `1997` = lifeExp[year == "1997"],
    `2002` = lifeExp[year == "2002"],
    `2007` = lifeExp[year == "2007"]
  ) |> # Creates the columns per country and year
  ungroup() |> # Remove the grouping
  mutate(change = `2007` - `1992`) # Adds a column to show the change in the data needed 

gap_slope_long <- gap_slope |> # Convert it to include all the data 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`1992`, `1997`, `2002`, `2007`),
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "lifeExp"
  ) # Reshape the data for easier use 

```

```{r}
ggplot(data = gap_slope_long, 
       aes(x = year, y = lifeExp, group = country, color = country)) +  # Set up the basic plot: x = year, y = life expectancy, group by country, color by country
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, show.legend = FALSE) +  # Draw lines connecting the points for each country, hide legend

  geom_label(
    aes(label = round(lifeExp, 0)),  # Add numbers inside the lines (life expectancy), rounded to 0 decimals
    size = 3.5,                      # Size of the text
    fill = "grey90",                  # Background color of the label
    color = "black",                  # Text color
    label.size = 0,                   # Remove the border around the label
    vjust = 0.5                       # Vertically center the text within the label
  ) +
   geom_segment(
    data = gap_slope_long |> filter(year == "1992"),
    aes(
      x = 0.85,          # slightly left of 1992 (which is position 1)
      xend = 1,           # connect to the 1992 point
      y = lifeExp,
      yend = lifeExp
    ),
    color = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  # RIGHT connecting lines (from 2007 point to country name)
  geom_segment(
    data = gap_slope_long |> filter(year == "2007"),
    aes(
      x = 4,              # 2007 position
      xend = 4.15,        # slightly to the right
      y = lifeExp,
      yend = lifeExp
    ),
    color = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  # Country labels on the left (1992)
  geom_text(
    data = gap_slope_long |> filter(year == "1992"),  # Only use 1992 data for left labels
    aes(label = country),                              # Text = country name
    hjust = 1,                                        # Align text to the right
    nudge_x = -0.15,                                  # Move text slightly to the left of the line
    size = 3,                                         # Smaller text size
    fontface = "bold",                                # Make text bold
    show.legend = FALSE                               # Do not show this in the legend
  ) +

  # Country labels on the right (2007)
  geom_text(
    data = gap_slope_long |> filter(year == "2007"),  # Only use 2007 data for right labels
    aes(label = country),                              # Text = country name
    hjust = -0.2,                                     # Align text slightly left (to keep space)
    nudge_x = 0.15,                                   # Move text slightly to the right of the line
    size = 3,                                         # Smaller text size
    fontface = "bold",                                # Make text bold
    show.legend = FALSE                               # Do not show this in the legend
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(values = c(                       # Manually set line colors for each country
    "Canada" = "dodgerblue3",
    "Puerto Rico" = "chartreuse4",
    "United States" = "yellow3",
    "Mexico" = "brown2",
    "El Salvador" = "darkorange",
    "Nicaragua" = "aquamarine3"
  )) +

  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +                 # Move the x-axis labels (years) to the top
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +                      # Allow labels to extend beyond plot edges

  labs(
    x = NULL,                                          # Remove x-axis label
    y = NULL,                                          # Remove y-axis label
    title = "Life Expectancy by Country",             # Main title
    subtitle = "Selected American countries",        # Subtitle
    caption = "source: gapminder"                     # Caption/source
  ) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "none",                          # Remove legend
    plot.margin = margin(10, 120, 10, 120),           # Add extra space on left/right for labels

    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = NA),  # Panel background
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = NA),   # Plot background

    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),                # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),                # Remove minor grid lines

    axis.text.y = element_blank(),                     # Remove y-axis numbers
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),                    # Remove y-axis ticks
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),                    # Remove x-axis ticks (years on top)

    axis.text.x = element_text(                        # Customize x-axis text
      face = "bold",                                   # Bold x-axis text
      size = rel(2)                                    # Make it larger relative to default
    ),

    plot.title = element_text(                         # Customize title
      hjust = 0.5,                                     # Center horizontally
      face = "bold"                                    # Bold title
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(                      # Customize subtitle
      hjust = 0.5,                                     # Center horizontally
      face = "italic"                                  # Italic subtitle
    )
  )
```




## Question 3. Area Charts

```{r}
pop <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/us_population_age_group_5yr_1900_2024_long.csv")

pop$age_group <- factor(pop$age_group, levels = rev(unique(pop$age_group)))

pop <- pop |>
  filter(age_group != "all",
         sex == "both")

ggplot(pop,
       aes(x = year,
           y = population / 1000,
           fill = fct_rev(age_group))) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1900, 2024, by = 10))+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d()+
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Population (in thousands)",
    fill = "Age Group",
    title = "US Population by age",
    subtitle = "1900 to 2024",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "italic")
   )

```





## Question 4. Stream Charts

```{r}
pop <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/us_population_age_group_5yr_1900_2024_long.csv")
pop_filtered <- pop %>% 
  filter(sex != "both",
         age_group != "all")

ggplot(pop_filtered,
       aes(x = year,
           y = population,
           fill = age_group)) +
  geom_stream(
    bw = 0.6, 
    type = "mirror"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ sex, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "magma") +
  # scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1920, 2020, 20),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL, 
    fill = "Age_Group",
    title = "US Population by age and sex",
    subtitle = "1900 to 2024"
  )

```




## Question 5. Alluvial Diagrams

```{r}
mtcars <- datasets::mtcars

df <- mtcars %>% 
  count(carb, cyl, gear, am) %>% 
  mutate(am= factor(am, levels=c(0,1), labels = c("Auto", "Man")))
ggplot(df, aes(y=n, axis1=carb, axis2=cyl, axis3=gear, axis4=am))+
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = carb),alpha = 0.5, color= "grey10")+
  geom_stratum(width = 0.4, color = "gray40", fill="grey95", alpha=.9)+
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 4)+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0), breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30))+
  scale_x_discrete(limits=c("Carburetors", "Cylinders", "Gears", "Transmission"), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c()+
  guides(fill="none")+
  labs(
    x = NULL, fill = NULL,
    y = "Frequency",
    title = "mtcars data",
    subtitle = "stratified by carb, cyl, gear, and am"
  )+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")  
  )

```

## Question 7. Correlation Heatmaps

```{r}
nba_players <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/nba_players_2022-23_2024-25.csv")

nba_cor <- nba_players |>
  select("salary", "g", "gs",
         "mp", "fg", "fga",
         "fg%", "3p", "3pa",
         "3p%", "2p", "2pa",
         "2p%", "efg%", "ft",
         "fta", "ft%", "orb",
         "drb", "trb", "ast",
         "stl", "blk", "tov",
         "pf", "pts") |>
  drop_na() |>
  cor()

p_mat <- nba_players |>
  select("salary", "g", "gs",
         "mp", "fg", "fga",
         "fg%", "3p", "3pa",
         "3p%", "2p", "2pa",
         "2p%", "efg%", "ft",
         "fta", "ft%", "orb",
         "drb", "trb", "ast",
         "stl", "blk", "tov",
         "pf", "pts") |>
  drop_na() |>
  cor_pmat()

ggcorrplot(
  nba_cor,
  method = "square",
  type = "lower",
  p.mat = p_mat,
  insig = "blank",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 2,
  colors = c("#4E79A7",
             "white",
             "#E15759"),
  title = "NBA Player Variables: Correlation Matrix"
)
```




## Question 8. Word Cloud

### Data

```{r}
x_cc_neg_weak <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/UStweets_negative_weak_2017.csv")
x_cc_neg_strong <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/UStweets_negative_strong_2017.csv")

# x_cc_neg_weak: tweets with weakly negative sentiment
# x_cc_neg_strong: tweets with strongly negative sentiment

# DT::datatable(x_cc_neg_weak)
# DT::datatable(x_cc_neg_strong)
```

### Text cleaning

```{r}
custom_remove <- c("climatechange", "globalwarming", "rt", "climate", "ll", "don")

  weak_top30 <- x_cc_neg_weak %>%
  
  # Remove any web links that start with http or https.
  # Example: "https://something.com"
  mutate(content = str_remove_all(content, "http[s]?://\\S+")) %>%
  
  # Remove Twitter image links specifically, such as pic.twitter.com/xxxxx
  mutate(content = str_remove_all(content, "pic\\.twitter\\.com/\\S+")) %>%
  
  # Replace anything that is NOT a letter or a space with a blank space.
  # This removes punctuation, numbers, symbols, emojis, etc.
  mutate(content = str_replace_all(content, "[^A-Za-z\\s]", " ")) %>%
  
  # Clean up spacing by shrinking repeated spaces into one space
  # and trimming extra spaces at the beginning/end.
  mutate(content = str_squish(content)) %>%
  
  # Break the text in the content column into individual words.
  # The new word column will hold one token (one word) per row.
  unnest_tokens(word, content) %>%
  
  # Remove common stop words like "the", "and", "is", etc.
  # This helps keep only more meaningful words.
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%
  filter(!word %in% custom_remove) %>%
  
  # Keep only words made of lowercase letters a-z.
  # This helps filter out weird leftovers or broken tokens.
  filter(str_detect(word, "^[a-z]+$")) %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)
  
  strong_top30 <- x_cc_neg_strong %>%
  mutate(content = str_remove_all(content, "http[s]?://\\S+")) %>%
  mutate(content = str_remove_all(content, "pic\\.twitter\\.com/\\S+")) %>%
  mutate(content = str_replace_all(content, "[^A-Za-z\\s]", " ")) %>%
  mutate(content = str_squish(content)) %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, content) %>%
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%
  filter(!word %in% custom_remove) %>%
  filter(str_detect(word, "^[a-z]+$")) %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)
```

### Word Clouds

### Josh

#### Preparing Words DataFrame

##### Weakly Negative Sentiments

```{r}
x_words_neg_weak <- x_cc_neg_weak %>% 
  filter(str_detect(content, regex("#climatechange|#globalwarming", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% 
  mutate(
    content = str_remove_all(content, "http[s]?://\\S+"),
    content = str_remove_all(content, "pic.twitter.com/\\S+"),
    content = str_remove_all(content, "t.co/\\S+"),
    content = str_replace_all(content, "'s|'re|'ve|'ll|'d|'t", ""),
    content = str_replace_all(content, "[^A-Za-z\\s]", " "),
    content = str_squish(content)
  ) %>% 
  unnest_tokens(word, content) %>% 
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>% 
  filter(!word %in% c(
    "climatechange", "globalwarming", "rt", "climate"
  )) %>% 
  filter(str_detect(word, "[a-z]")) %>% 
  count(word, sort = TRUE) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 30)
```

##### Weakly Negative Sentiments Plot

```{r}
x_words_neg_weak %>% 
  ggplot(aes(label = word,
             size = n,
             color = n)) +
  geom_text_wordcloud_area(
    shape = "square",
    grid_size = 1) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 30) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_b()
```
